[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
Medium format 6x7 documentary architectural photograph taken with a Mamiya 7 and 45mm wide-angle rectilinear lens on fine-grain film at f/8. An elevated wide-angle view overlooking the Thomas Jefferson Memorial on the southern shore of the Tidal Basin in Washington, D.C., aligned along the north-south monumental axis toward the Washington Monument obelisk in the background. The Jefferson Memorial displays a circular Classical rotunda composed of Vermont Imperial Danby white marble fluted Ionic columns, a concentric attic, and a stepped shallow hemispherical dome clad in Indiana oolitic limestone. All architectural lines are perfectly planarized and plumbed to true gravity vertical. Subtle, authentic micro-environmental weathering, faint calcite veining, and delicate rainwater patina mark the marble masonry and cornice joints. Surrounding the monument are lush, organic groves of mature Yoshino cherry trees and American elms with dense green leafy canopies, contrasting with manicured grass berms, asphalt curving access drives, and dressed pink granite seawalls along the smooth water of the Tidal Basin.
